basis: Acute myeloid leukemia involving blood and marrow; the chromosomal subtype does not establish another commonly damaged organ.
Diffuse mucin deposition in skin; no evidence establishes common functional damage outside the skin.
Malignant neoplasm occupying the spinal cord; lymphoma is only one subtype of this umbrella concept.
Premature ovarian insufficiency is failure of gonadal endocrine function; uterine hypoplasia and amenorrhea add no separate axis.
Intellectual disability and developmental delay characterize affected patients; other organ defects vary by duplicated interval and sex.
Menstrual-cycle disorder of the reproductive system; no endocrine disease or other covered organ damage is established by this umbrella.
Open spinal dysraphism affects cord and vertebral arches; neurogenic bladder and bowel cause persistent dysfunction in most patients (>50% each).
Lipomatous tethering damages spinal roots; bladder dysfunction and structural foot deformities are common (~30%+). Bowel dysfunction frequency is less certain.
Congenital fusion of digits defines this skeletal developmental disorder; syndromic extra-organ findings do not apply across the umbrella.
Immune-mediated Crohn inflammation directly damages the jejunum; extraintestinal complications are not established as common for this subtype.
Selective tooth agenesis with oligodontia in 4/4 patients; other reported structural features occur in only 1/4.
Defined by disease of the superficial cutaneous vasculature; immune mechanisms and systemic organ damage are subtype-dependent.
Disordered ether-lipid synthesis causes a neurologic syndrome; early cataracts are characteristic and reported in most affected patients (>80%).
Gingival overgrowth, anonychia and intellectual disability each 2/2; sensorineural hearing loss 1/2. Kyphosis 1/2 omitted by cap; hypotonia alone adds no muscle axis.
Acute malignant proliferation of megakaryoblasts in marrow and blood; no other organ has established common direct damage.
Renal dysgenesis, thymic aplasia and anal atresia define the syndrome; lung dysplasia is a named core malformation, with frequency unreported.
Localized cartilaginous outgrowth of the posterior pinna; the external ear belongs to the otologic axis.
Immune-mediated eosinophilic inflammation of skin; reactive blood eosinophilia does not establish a separate hematologic disease.
Inherited factor IX deficiency causes abnormal bleeding; chronic joint damage is not established in ≥30% of this moderate-severity subtype.
Predisposition principally to breast and reproductive cancers, outside the axes; pancreatic cancer and melanoma are separate cancers and minority risks.
Congenital absence of the lower central incisors; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Histoplasma infection principally arises in the lungs; disseminated CNS, ocular and other organ disease does not characterize most patients.
EBV-associated B-cell lymphoma predominantly involving lungs; CNS infiltration occurs in ~30–40%. Cutaneous infiltration (~30–40%) omitted by cap.
Neoplasm occupying the pleura; organs of origin of metastatic tumors vary and are not inherent to this concept.
Rhizomelic skeletal dysplasia, callosal agenesis/hydrocephalus and thrombocytopenia define the syndrome; hypertension is also a defining feature.
